courses.title: Healthful Living
courses.description: A comprehensive look at factors that impact people's health, longevity and lifetime wellness designed for Kinesiology majors and general education students. Emphasis is placed on individual responsibility for personal health and the promotion of informed, positive health behaviors. Essential components of health and wellness include: nutrition, exercise, weight control, eating disorders, body image, mental health, stress management, violence, substance abuse, reproductive health, sexuality, disease prevention, aging, healthcare, media influence, and environmental hazards and safety. CSU/UC

courses.subject: KNHE
courses.title: Women's Health Issues
courses.description: An investigation into traditional and holistic health topics with a special emphasis on women's issues, considering all aspects and concepts of social and political influences, nutrition and fitness, relationships, sexuality, reproductive issues, and careers. This course analyzes the biological, psychological, and sociocultural aspects of women's health and explores health services, health education, and healthcare delivery systems. Women's role in family, workforce, community, and society as well as strategies for social and political change are explored. CSU/UC

courses.subject: KNHE
courses.title: Men's Health Issues
courses.description: Examines the societal, economic, cultural, and gender influences that shape men's health beliefs and practices. Explores specific health issues unique to men such as accessing health care, healthy relationships, domestic abuse, prostate cancer, and alcohol use. Critically examines literature and media to identify interventions within a masculinity framework to improve men's health outcomes. Identification of positive outcomes of healthy men at home, work, and in society. CSU/UC

courses.subject: KNHE

courses.subject: KNHE
courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and First Aid
courses.description: This course involves the theory and detailed demonstration of the first aid care of the injured. The student will learn to assess a victim's condition and incorporate proper treatment. Standard first aid, CPR, and AED certification(s) will be granted upon successful completion of requirements. CSU/UC

courses.subject: KNHE
courses.title: Stress Management
courses.description: This course covers theoretical and research-based frameworks of stress, stress response, and stress management techniques. Topics include the definition of stress, physiological and psychological effects of stress, sources and causes of stress, and health consequences of chronic stress. Numerous evidence-based techniques to manage and cope with stress will also be covered and practiced. CSU/UC

courses.subject: KNHE
courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.description: This course presents an overview of the disciplines of community and public health. Topics include the basic concepts and terminologies of public health; an overview of various public health professions and organizations; the study, prevention and control of diseases in the community; the analysis of the social determinants of health; strategies for eliminating disease, illness, and health disparities among various populations; community organizing and health promotion programming; school health promotion; environmental health and safety; and an overview of the healthcare delivery system in the United States. Emphasis will be placed on the development of knowledge and preliminary skills to serve as an effective advocate for community and public health. CSU/UC

courses.subject: KNHE
courses.title: Health and Social Justice
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the health inequities in the United States that stem from unequal living conditions. Students will explore how education, socioeconomic status, racism, and gender shape health epidemics and policy development. Fundamental theories to advocate for health and social justice will be explored, and community organizing approaches will be practiced. CSU/UC

courses.subject: KNHE
courses.title: Drugs, Health, and Society
courses.description: This course explains concepts and theories relating to the epidemiology and toxicology of substance use, misuse, abuse, and dependence, and the impact on personal, community and societal health. The biological/physiological, neurological, and psychological short and long-term effects of selected pharmacological substances on the human brain and body are explored, including an analysis of risk factors associated with abuse and dependence. Historical, political, social, socioeconomic, and legal factors involved in the practice, marketing, distribution, and government regulations of legal and illegal drugs will be covered. An overview of contemporary methods used in prevention, diagnosis and treatment will be reviewed, including an analysis of effective evidence-based strategies and local recovery resources. CSU

courses.title: Sport and Society
courses.description: Examines the role of sport in modern society. Looks at how sport influences and shapes global attitudes among nations. Investigates the historical, social, economic, and political impact of sport on society. CSU/UC

courses.title: Theory of Soccer
courses.description: This course is designed for the competitive soccer player. Students will learn and develop a further understanding of the game of soccer. Laws of the game, offensive and defensive techniques and tactics, and the physical preparation for becoming a soccer player will be discussed. CSU/UC

courses.title: Sport Psychology Applications - Soccer
courses.description: This course provides advanced mental training to improve soccer performance. Theories, strategies, and best practices include; mental set, arousal and performance, mental imagery, and motivation as they pertain to preparing for soccer competition. Students will develop necessary knowledge and skills to prepare for intercollegiate competition as well as self-assess readiness for transfer and the selection of transfer program. Open Entry/Open Exit. CSU

Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
